s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of swelling and pain in the right foot/ankle with associated fevers and systemic symptoms, in a patient with a history of a condition diagnosed at a young age and evidence of chronic skin and soft tissue abnormalities
salient_findings: Hardened plaque and depigmentation on the face, chest, and abdomen
Hardened nodules and masses on the upper extremities
key_facts: 31-year-old African American man
Originally from the Togolese Republic
Presented with right foot/ankle swelling and pain
Associated fevers began the morning before presenting
Medical history includes a condition diagnosed at 8 years old
Tachycardic, diaphoretic, and febrile
Hardened plaque and depigmentation on the face, chest, and abdomen
Hardened nodules and masses on the upper extremities
Right foot/ankle was fluctuant and tender to palpation
Normal renal function
Leukocytosis (WBC count: 18.7 × 10³/UL)
Elevated total creatine kinase (1947 U/L)
Normal corrected calcium (9.62 mg/dL)
Depressed phosphorus (1.7 mg/dL)
Normal lactic acid (1.7 mmol/L) and magnesium (1.9 mg/dL)
X-ray and CT scan showed soft tissue calcifications

shortlist.label: Tumoral Calcinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with soft tissue calcifications, fluctuant and tender right foot/ankle, and a history of a condition diagnosed at a young age, which are consistent with tumoral calcinosis

shortlist.label: Familial Tumoral Calcinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to tumoral calcinosis, the patient's symptoms and history could suggest a familial form of the disease, especially given the early age of diagnosis of a condition

shortlist.label: Calcinosis Cutis
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's presentation of soft tissue calcifications and hardened plaque with depigmentation could be indicative of calcinosis cutis, a condition characterized by calcium deposits in the skin

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: The combination of skin manifestations (hardened plaque and depigmentation) and elevated creatine kinase suggests dermatomyositis, an inflammatory disease that affects the skin and muscles

shortlist.label: Normophosphatemic Familial Tumoral Calcinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Given the patient's normal phosphorus levels and the presence of soft tissue calcifications, normophosphatemic familial tumoral calcinosis is a plausible diagnosis, considering the familial aspect and the specific biochemical profile

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of soft tissue calcifications, fluctuant and tender right foot/ankle, and elevated creatine kinase levels are consistent with Tumoral Calcinosis, which is characterized by the formation of calcified masses in soft tissues.

rejected.label: Calcinosis Cutis
rejected.why: Calcinosis Cutis typically presents with calcified lesions in the skin, but does not typically involve deep soft tissue calcifications as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While Dermatomyositis can present with skin manifestations and elevated creatine kinase, it does not typically involve soft tissue calcifications.

rejected.label: Familial Tumoral Calcinosis
rejected.why: Familial Tumoral Calcinosis is a rare genetic disorder, and while the patient has a medical history since age 8, there is no clear indication of a familial component in this case.

rejected.label: Normophosphatemic Familial Tumoral Calcinosis
rejected.why: The patient's phosphorus level is depressed, which does not align with the normophosphatemic characteristic of this condition.
